caption_fb:
Why does Great-Grandpa's record say "Austria"?

From 1795 to 1918, Poland wasn't on the map. Its land was split between Russia, Prussia and Austria, so American records often name the empire, not Poland. The 1900 census even told clerks to write "Poland (Russ.)," "Poland (Aust.)" or "Poland (Ger.)."

What it can tell you:
🔹 "Austria" usually points to Galicia, today's southern Poland
🔹 "Russia" usually points to central or eastern Poland
🔹 "Germany" or "Prussia" usually points to western or northern Poland

Your next step: list every record that names a country, spelled the way it's written. Each spelling is a clue.
